The Celestial Church of Christ is an African-initiated church founded in 1947 in Porto-Novo, in what was then French Dahomey and is now Benin, by Samuel Oshoffa. It has spread across West Africa and to African communities in Europe and the Americas.

Oshoffa was a carpenter. He said that while lost in the forest during an eclipse he received a vision calling him to found a church. He became known for healing, and his followers saw him as a prophet.

The church belongs to the Aladura family of prayer churches that arose in Yoruba lands from the 1920s, blending Protestant Christianity with African ways of worship. Members wear white robes and worship barefoot. Prayer, visions, prophecy and healing are at the centre, and alcohol and tobacco are forbidden.

The church grew fast in Nigeria, especially around Lagos, home to many of its largest parishes. Like the church of Simon Kimbangu in the Congo, it shows how Africans built their own forms of Christianity apart from the mission churches.
